column3: “A scroll of a document” is rendered “a scroll.”
“From the mouth of” is rendered “at the dictation of.”
“From my mouth” is rendered “at my dictation.”
“May their supplication fall” is rendered “come before.”
“They were in dread each to his neighbor” is rendered “turned in fear one to another.”
NASB adds the question “Was it at his dictation?” where the Hebrew has “from his mouth.”
“From his mouth he proclaimed” is rendered “He dictated,” and “the scroll” as “the book.”
“Doors” is rendered “columns,” and NASB supplies “the king.”
